movies.title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 Quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
movies.description: A magnificent epic of experimental cinema offering a feminist perspective on recurrent events of everyday life.

movies.title: Vertigo
movies.description: A former detective with a fear of heights is hired to follow a woman apparently possessed by the past, in Alfred Hitchcock’s timeless thriller about obsession.

movies.title: Citizen Kane
movies.description: Famously sitting at the top of the Sight and Sound Greatest Films of All Time poll from 1962 to 2002, Orson Welles’s debut, about newspaper magnate Charles Foster Kane, remains an enduring classic.

movies.title: Tokyo Story
movies.description: Told in Yasujirō Ozu’s simple and elegant style, this story of intergenerational discord is heartbreaking and deeply human.

movies.title: In the Mood for Love
movies.description: Wong Kar Wai’s masterpiece is a heartbreaking story of illicit love that pulses with the ache of repressed desire.

movies.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
movies.description: Stanley Kubrick’s grand vision of mankind’s journey from its hominid beginnings to its star-child evolution is a towering achievement of science-fiction cinema.

movies.title: Beau travail
movies.description: Claire Denis’s great gift is to evoke emotion with gesture and juxtaposition. In the desert, water shimmers and ripples, naked shoulders perspire, black mosquito nets recall sheer lingerie.

movies.title: Mulholland Dr.
movies.description: Hollywood is dark and dangerous, yet alluring, in David Lynch’s acclaimed thriller.

movies.title: Man with a Movie Camera
movies.description: Bottomless invention and frenetic, dizzying montage make this city symphony one of cinema’s sharpest, most exciting experiences nearly a century after its release.

movies.title: Singin' in the Rain
movies.description: Hollywood’s troubled transition from silent to talking pictures at the end of the 1920s provided the inspiration for perhaps the greatest of movie musicals.

movies.title: Sunrise A Song of Two Humans
movies.description: The first American film by one of German expressionism’s leading exponents, this lush, atmospheric silent drama is replete with groundbreaking cinematography.

movies.title: The Godfather
movies.description: The first of Francis Ford Coppola’s epic trilogy about the Corleone crime family is the disturbing story of a son drawn inexorably into his father’s Mafia affairs.

movies.title: La Règle du jeu
movies.description: Huge-spirited and sharp-eyed, Jean Renoir’s French-society fresco gathers high classes and low for a weekend of country-house fallout.

movies.title: Cléo from 5 to 7
movies.description: In real time, Cléo becomes more real, more subject than object. She discards her whipped-cream wig and polka dots for a simple black shift. She performs less and feels more.

movies.title: The Searchers
movies.description: This poll’s last western standing, John Ford’s sweeping, stirring rescue-or-revenge quest remains a film of magnificent mystery and poetry.

movies.title: Meshes of the Afternoon
movies.description: Had Californian sunlight ever looked as suggestive or sinister before the sharply etched dreamworld of Meshes of the Afternoon?

movies.title: Close-up
movies.description: The more ‘information’ we’re offered about the case, the more we come to realise that there are no easy answers to any of the questions being raised.

movies.title: Persona
movies.description: Any sense of a conventional psychodrama is constantly disrupted by the experimental, improvisatory filmmaking.

movies.title: Apocalypse Now
movies.description: Francis Ford Coppola’s Vietnam War blowout, a hell-trip through the smoke and dazzle of imperial America’s most grandstanding rogue show.

movies.title: Seven Samurai
movies.description: Akira Kurosawa’s monumental, scintillating tale of hired samurai protecting a peasant village: period thriller and moral/political fable in one.

movies.title: Late Spring
movies.description: The first of Yasujirō Ozu’s great cycle of dramas that place the joys and sadnesses of family life in the context of a Japan disrupted by modernity.

movies.title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
movies.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer’s rapturous silent masterpiece, with soulful close-ups of Renée Jeanne “Maria” Falconetti’s tremulous martyr, transcending tyranny and temporality.

movies.title: Playtime
movies.description: Jacques Tati’s most painstaking accomplishment blends deft slapstick, endless visual ingenuity and sonic comedy in a stupendous modern satire.

movies.title: Do the Right Thing
movies.description: Racial tensions reach boiling point in Spike Lee’s incandescent portrait of a Brooklyn neighbourhood on the hottest day of the year.

movies.title: Au hasard Balthazar
movies.description: Robert Bresson gave us a typically stark vision of humanity as experienced by a put-upon, maltreated beast of burden that passes from owner to owner.

movies.title: The Night of the Hunter
movies.description: Actor Charles Laughton’s only film as director, starring Robert Mitchum as an implacable child-hunting preacher, still leaves an indelible mark.

movies.title: Shoah
movies.description: To make sense of the 20th century’s most horrific atrocity, Claude Lanzmann reinvented documentary itself, giving the form colossal new significance.

movies.title: Daisies
movies.description: This feminist milestone is an anarchic comedy of subversion whose approach to montage is as exuberant as the film’s two protagonists.

movies.title: Taxi Driver
movies.description: Martin Scorsese and Paul Schrader’s high-art vigilante movie for fallen times, with a coiled Robert De Niro as psycho-saviour of an infernal NYC.

movies.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
movies.description: Portrait of a Lady on Fire demonstrates Céline Sciamma’s ability to make a timelessly beautiful film that also crystallises the gender politics of her era.

movies.title: 8½
movies.description: Federico Fellini’s portrait of the film director as harried ringmaster and unreliable dreamer, spinning gold from his memories and fantasies.

movies.title: Mirror
movies.description: Cinema scaled new heights of visual poetry in this deeply personal, elliptical film by the master of ‘sculpting in time’.

movies.title: Psycho
movies.description: Alfred Hitchcock’s unsparing wrong-motel shocker starring Janet Leigh is a watershed for mainstream horror and still seminal in its suspense games.

movies.title: L'Atalante
movies.description: Jean Vigo’s headily poetic portrait of young newlyweds on – and off – Michel Simon’s barge on the Seine.

movies.title: Pather Panchali
movies.description: All the mischief, discoveries, joys and tragedies of life are given endlessly lyrical expression in Satyajit Ray’s debut, the first entry in ‘The Apu Trilogy’.

movies.title: City Lights
movies.description: A purely beautiful outing from the Tramp, this delightful urban romance features one of cinema’s most heartbreaking smiles.

movies.title: M
movies.description: Fritz Lang’s rack-taut first talkie, with a searing, animalistic Peter Lorre as a serial child-murderer turned manhunt target.

movies.title: Rear Window
movies.description: The Master of Suspense ratchets up the tension while dishing out insights into obsession, urban living and the dangers of the gaze.

movies.title: Some Like It Hot
movies.description: Billy Wilder’s supreme gender-bending comedy has Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis as female-posing musicians on the lam, and many knickers in a twist.

movies.title: À bout de souffle
movies.description: Jean-Luc Godard’s cock-of-the-walk calling card, mixing pulp pastiche and upstart rebellion with Jean-Paul Belmondo’s footloose Parisian delinquent.

movies.title: Bicycle Thieves
movies.description: The film that topped Sight and Sound’s inaugural Greatest Films of All Time poll in 1952, Vittorio De Sica’s indelible neorealist parable offers a sharp-eyed portrait of Italy’s post-war privations.

movies.title: Rashomon
movies.description: The film that brought Japanese cinema to the world, this 88-minute firecracker proved a seminal assault on the notion of objectivity.

movies.title: Killer of Sheep
movies.description: Charles Burnett’s tender and witty tale of a disillusioned slaughterhouse worker and the solace to be found in the simplest moments of life.

movies.title: Stalker
movies.description: Two men recruit a guide to take them into ‘the Zone’, a mysterious realm where one’s innermost wishes come true, in this metaphysical sci-fi epic.

movies.title: Barry Lyndon
movies.description: Stanley Kubrick’s meticulously designed epic recounts the picaresque exploits of an 18th-century Irish adventurer.

movies.title: North by Northwest
movies.description: Insouciant big-screen thrill-games from the Master of Suspense, hounding Cary Grant’s smug adman across a continent’s span of peerless set pieces.

movies.title: The Battle of Algiers
movies.description: A window on Algeria’s wider liberation war, recreating a violent phase of guerrilla struggle and suppression in powerful free-documentary style.

movies.title: Ordet
movies.description: An austere parable on the power of faith, Carl Theodor Dreyer’s penultimate film culminates in a transcendent resurrection scene.

movies.title: Wanda
movies.description: Barbara Loden’s tough, unsentimental portrait of a woman adrift in the industrial heartlands of the north-eastern United States.

movies.title: The 400 Blows
movies.description: François Truffaut’s free-wheeling debut, with Jean-Pierre Léaud as his rebel-schoolboy surrogate, is still a banner film for nouvelle vague lyric realism.

movies.title: The Piano
movies.description: This virtuoso drama of a mute woman’s and her daughter’s silent defiance of patriarchy in 19th-century New Zealand still has searing emotional heft.

movies.title: Fear Eats the Soul
movies.description: Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s heart-on-sleeve melodrama of a doomed romance across racial and age divides probes social hypocrisy with feeling.

movies.title: News from Home
movies.description: Chantal Akerman’s epistolary film, shot in the grime of 70s New York, bridges the distance from Brussels through dictated letters from her mother.

movies.title: Battleship Potemkin
movies.description: Sergei Eisenstein’s renowned agit-drama of proto-revolutionary mutiny and repression, often quoted but still powerful in its montage effects.

movies.title: Blade Runner
movies.description: Iconic neo-noir in a befouled sci-fi Los Angeles where humans and their machine replicas vie to be predators rather than prey.

movies.title: Le Mépris
movies.description: Disillusion in love and cinema in Jean-Luc Godard’s most opulent and emotive production, with lovers and film legends at loggerheads in Capri.

movies.title: Sherlock Jr.
movies.description: Buster Keaton’s would-be sleuth dreams himself into movie-heroic mastery in this dazzling, evergreen, meta masterpiece of silent comedy.

movies.title: The Apartment
movies.description: Billy Wilder’s then-risqué romcom, with Jack Lemmon and Shirley Maclaine finding love amid corporate New York’s sea of sexual deception.

movies.title: Sans soleil
movies.description: Chris Marker’s speculative travelogue-essay, reflecting on culture and history in narrated letters from Guinea to Japan to Iceland.

movies.title: Daughters of the Dust
movies.description: Julie Dash’s visionary visual marriage between Afrocentric aesthetics and the rich emotional depth of Black womanhood is a cinematic triumph.

movies.title: La dolce vita
movies.description: Federico Fellini’s ode to Rome presents a lush, vibrant exterior to the swinging city, before revealing its rotting moral core.

movies.title: Moonlight
movies.description: Instantly heralded as a modern masterpiece, Barry Jenkins’ stunning three-part story of queer identity is both a technical and an emotional marvel.

movies.title: Casablanca
movies.description: Ingrid Bergman rallies Humphrey Bogart’s embittered cynic to the anti-Nazi cause in this classic romance.

movies.title: GoodFellas
movies.description: The dizzying story of wiseguy Henry Hill, from his seduction into a life of crime to his paranoid, cocaine-fuelled departure.

movies.title: The Third Man
movies.description: Joseph Cotten chases Orson Welles’s agent of corruption through the ruins of divided post-war Vienna in this evocative classic thriller.

movies.title: Touki Bouki
movies.description: A restless young couple dream of escaping Senegal for Paris in Djibril Diop Mambéty ’s stylish, poetic, irreverent expression of post-colonial fantasies.

movies.title: Andrei Rublev
movies.description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s epic portrait of a medieval artist may be the most wrenching depiction of belief, creativity and the search for meaning ever filmed.

movies.title: La Jetée
movies.description: The rare short film in this list, Marker’s dazzling photo montage ruminates on memory from beyond the apocalypse.

movies.title: Metropolis
movies.description: Fritz Lang’s bombastic, stylised depiction of a future of profound inequality has influenced generations of genre filmmakers.

movies.title: The Gleaners and I
movies.description: Agnès Varda’s essay portrait of society ’s scavenger-recyclers – herself included – is both free-radical and infectious.

movies.title: The Red Shoes
movies.description: The feverish Technicolor and astonishing ballet sequences for which this film is so renowned are as spellbinding as they are disturbing.

movies.title: Journey to Italy
movies.description: Roberto Rossellini’s plaintively simple portrait of a marriage on the rocks, imprinted with the ghosts of love, cultures and civilisations.

movies.title: L'avventura
movies.description: Michelangelo Antonioni’s high-modernist breakthrough sends Monica Vitti in search less of her disappeared friend than her own self, via images to get lost in.

movies.title: My Neighbour Totoro
movies.description: The storytelling is as simple as Totoro is inscrutable, unfolding in a series of delightful, exquisitely constructed sequences.

movies.title: Imitation of Life
movies.description: Douglas Sirk’s melodrama holds a mirror to the hypocrisies of 1950s America with its pairs of mothers and daughters across class and racial divides.

movies.title: Sansho the Bailiff
movies.description: Kenji Mizoguchi’s tragic folk saga of the tribulations of an exiled governor’s family in feudal Japan, tracked with exquisitely moving camerawork.

movies.title: Spirited Away
movies.description: Hayao Miyazaki’s rich anime fantasy follows its ten-year-old heroine into the labyrinth of a spirit-world bathhouse, teeming with phantoms and peril.

movies.title: A Brighter Summer Day
movies.description: Young love and teen delinquency in Taiwan’s early 1960s adolescence, in Edward Yang’s slow-burn, bittersweet epic.

movies.title: A Matter of Life and Death
movies.description: Love is rescued from the jaws of the afterlife in the Archers’ delirious World War II air-pilot fantasia.

movies.title: Céline and Julie Go Boating
movies.description: Jacques Rivette’s most playful, innovative frolic, in which his irreverent Parisian heroines dissolve worlds, genres, social codes and boundaries.

movies.title: Histoire(s) du Cinéma
movies.description: The apotheosis of Jean-Luc Godard’s experimental era, this sprawling essay film indicts the 20th century through its most popular medium.

movies.title: Modern Times
movies.description: Industrial modernity proves mercilessly madcap in Charlie Chaplin’s final (mostly) silent feature, one of the most inspired and ingenious of all his comedies.

movies.title: Sunset Blvd.
movies.description: Tinseltown’s greatest self-satire, a gothic requiem for big-screen bygones and the highs of screen stardom.

movies.title: Sátántangó
movies.description: As timely as ever in its grim poeticisation of demagogues and doom, helplessness and hope. If music be the food of death, play on.

movies.title: Blue Velvet
movies.description: David Lynch’s adult fairytale follows teen sleuth Kyle MacLachlan’s murder inquiry into the surreal, perverse corners of small-town America.

movies.title: Pierrot le fou
movies.description: Jean-Luc Godard’s most effervescent escapade, a primary-coloured lovers-on-the-run blow-out heading south with Anna Karina and Jean-Paul Belmondo.

movies.title: The Spirit of the Beehive
movies.description: Victor Erice’s exquisite impressionistic distillation of childhood fear and wonder in the ruins of the recently ended Spanish Civil War.

movies.title: CHUNGKING EXPRESS
movies.description: A sense of wistful, romantic longing joins the two stories in Wong Kar Wai’s freewheeling portmanteau portrait of Hong Kong.

movies.title: The Shining
movies.description: Stanley Kubrick’s much analysed and often spoofed psychological horror spends a chilling and claustrophobic winter at the empty Overlook Hotel.

movies.title: Madame de...
movies.description: Max Ophuls’ woozy whirligig tracks a pair of unwanted earrings around high-society Paris – until they bear the weight of lost time and passion.

movies.title: Parasite
movies.description: Like Get Out, Bong Joon Ho’s endlessly twisty, blackly sincere class-war thriller is a pop provocation for our unequal times.

movies.title: The Leopard
movies.description: Luchino Visconti’s sumptuous epic portrays the fall of 19th-century Sicilian nobility, its decadent displays of wealth tinged with melancholy.

movies.title: Ugetsu Monogatari
movies.description: Kenji Mizoguchi’s bewitching, insinuating Edo-period ghost story renders civil war as a parable of heedless male greed.

movies.title: Yi Yi
movies.description: Urban anomie and multi-generational growing pains are given rich, relaxed expression in Edward Yang’s heartfelt Taipei family tapestry.

movies.title: A Man Escaped
movies.description: This prison-break study is Robert Bresson at his most starkly essential: a man, four walls, his ingenuity and the mysterious inflections of fate.

movies.title: Black Girl
movies.description: Ousmane Sembène lifts the mask on France’s racist post-colonial relationship with Senegal in his small yet commanding feature debut.

movies.title: Get Out
movies.description: A poster film for Black Lives Matter, Jordan Peele’s horror-satire of white vampirism gleefully needles America’s racial malaise.

movies.title: Once upon a Time in the West
movies.description: Sergio Leone’s operatic widescreen elegy to the old American West, with the forces of corporate capitalism coming down the railroad.

movies.title: The General
movies.description: Buster Keaton’s most lavish production and his warmest, bringing together a boy, a girl and a train amid the maelstrom of the US Civil War.

movies.title: Tropical Malady
movies.description: A work that defies straightforward understanding and suggests understandability may be overrated.

movies.title: Rio Bravo
movies.description: A decade after Red River (1947), Howard Hawks reteamed with John Wayne for this rambling western riffing on the director’s usual themes of friendship and professionalism.

movies.title: Jaws
movies.description: Steven Spielberg laid the template for the modern summer blockbuster with this expert thriller about the hunt for a man-eating great white shark.

movies.title: The Godfather Part II
movies.description: The expansive second part of Francis Ford Coppola’s Mafia saga continues the Corleone family story, charting in parallel young Vito’s earlier rise to prominence.

movies.title: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
movies.description: The coming of civilisation brings an end to the wildness of the west in John Ford’s elegiac late film teaming John Wayne and James Stewart.

movies.title: The Wizard of Oz
movies.description: Whisked by a tornado from Kansas to the colourful Land of Oz, Dorothy soon learns there’s no place like home in MGM’s immortal musical fantasy.

movies.title: Touch of Evil
movies.description: Orson Welles’ return to Hollywood after ten years working in Europe is a sleazy border tale in which he takes centre stage as gargantuan detective Hank Quinlan.

movies.title: Wild Strawberries
movies.description: On a road trip to receive an honorary degree, an elderly academic (Victor Sjöstrom) looks back over his life in Ingmar Bergman’s art-cinema classic.

movies.title: Don't Look Now
movies.description: Set in off-season Venice, British director Nicolas Roeg’s tragedy combines an acute study of grief with a supernaturally charged thriller plot, to beautiful and devastating effect.

movies.title: Nashville
movies.description: Made to celebrate the bicentennial of American Independence, Robert Altman’s footloose epic blends the lives of 24 characters in the capital of country music.

movies.title: To Be or Not to Be
movies.description: Ernst Lubitsch’s audacious farce, satirising ‘the Nazis and their ridiculous ideology’.

movies.title: Aguirre, Wrath of God
movies.description: Werner Herzog’s visceral exploration of doomed adventure and savage beauty is one of German cinema’s totemic masterpieces.

movies.title: The Conformist
movies.country: Italy, France, Federal Republic of Germany
movies.description: Bernardo Bertolucci’s stylish period thriller stars Jean-Louis Trintignant as a repressed bureaucrat in Mussolini’s Italy who is assigned to kill his former professor.

movies.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
movies.description: Unrivalled in its relentless vision of pure terror, Tobe Hooper’s horror masterpiece remains as brutal and horrific as it ever was.

movies.title: The Thing
movies.description: Twelve men at an Antarctic research station battle a shape-shifting alien that hides in human form, in John Carpenter’s groundbreaking sci-fi horror.

movies.title: Johnny Guitar
movies.description: Joan Crawford and Mercedes McCambridge excel in this fascinatingly strange Nicholas Ray western that takes in both sexual rivalry and xenophobia.

movies.title: Only Angels Have Wings
movies.description: Danger, desire, death and a donkey – Cary Grant, Jean Arthur and Rita Hayworth are flying high in Howard Hawks's peerlessly entertaining tale of aviation in the Andes.

movies.title: The Colour of Pomegranates
movies.description: The film that Martin Scorsese compared to ‘opening a door and walking into another dimension, where time has stopped and beauty has been unleashed’.

movies.title: The Matrix
movies.description: The Wachowksi sisters’ virtual-reality science-fiction epic marked a new high for effects-driven action sequences, and eventually launched a trilogy.

movies.title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
movies.description: Jacques Demy’s all-sung tale of first love is a ravishing mix of music, romance and fertile cinematic invention.

movies.title: There Will Be Blood
movies.description: This operatic portrait of a diabolical oil baron is a formal tour de force and a compelling portrait of all-American 20th century sociopathy.

movies.title: Fanny and Alexander
movies.country: Sweden, France, Federal Republic of Germany
movies.description: The grand summation of Ingmar Bergman’s career, this epic family drama drew on the director’s own childhood experiences in early 20th century Sweden.

movies.title: His Girl Friday
movies.description: A newspaper editor manipulates all around him for the sake of a scoop in one of the fastest and funniest comedies ever made.

movies.title: Pulp Fiction
movies.description: Quentin Tarantino’s crackling crime classic still retains its swagger as one of the great American films of the 1990s.

movies.title: Raging Bull
movies.description: Starring Robert De Niro as the middleweight boxer Jake La Motta, Martin Scorsese’s biopic is widely acknowledged as one of the greatest films of the 1980s.

movies.title: It's a Wonderful Life
movies.description: Undervalued on its initial release, this small-town drama has become a Christmas favourite, though its tearful affirmation is laced with darker emotions.

movies.title: Lawrence of Arabia
movies.description: An eccentric English officer inspires the Arabs to unite against the Turks during WWI in David Lean’s seven Oscar-winner, an epic in every sense.

movies.title: Notorious
movies.description: In one of Alfred Hitchcock’s darkest thrillers, a traitor’s daughter is engaged by an American agent to get close to one of her father’s Nazi associates.

movies.title: All That Heaven Allows
movies.description: Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson star in Douglas Sirk’s influential melodrama.

movies.title: Gertrud
movies.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer’s final masterpiece centres on a woman who rejects the compromise of her marriage and retreats into a serene isolation.

movies.title: La ciénaga
movies.country: Argentina, USA, Japan, France, Switzerland, Spain, Brazil

movies.title: Les Enfants du paradis
movies.description: Made during the Nazi occupation of France, Marcel Carne’s romantic epic of the 19th-century theatre world is a life-affirming tribute to love, Paris and the stage.

movies.title: Partie de campagne
movies.description: On a country picnic, a young girl leaves her family for a while and succumbs to an all-too-brief romance in Jean Renoir's sensuous tribute to the countryside.

movies.title: Pickpocket
movies.description: Robert Bresson’s hugely influential study of a petty thief in late 1950s Paris is one of his most widely acclaimed films.

movies.title: Sambizanga
movies.description: A riveting neorealist testimony to Angola’s anti-colonialist struggle, not screened there until after independence.

movies.title: The Seventh Seal
movies.description: During the plague-ravaged middle ages, a knight buys time for himself by playing chess with Death in Ingmar Bergman’s much-imitated arthouse classic.

movies.title: The Wild Bunch
movies.description: A gang of outlaws goes out in a blaze of violence and glory in Sam Peckinpah’s elegiac film about the dying days of the wild west.

movies.title: Alien
movies.description: The crew of mining spaceship Nostromo answer an apparent distress signal and find themselves with an unwanted passenger, in Ridley Scott’s breakthrough sci-fi horror.

movies.title: Chinatown
movies.description: Roman Polanski’s brilliant thriller stars Jack Nicholson as a private eye uncovering corruption in 1930s Los Angeles, a desert town where water equals power.

movies.title: La Grande Illusion
movies.description: Jean Renoir’s pacifist classic is set in a German prisoner-of-war camp during WWI, where class kinship is felt across national boundaries.

movies.title: The Watermelon Woman
movies.description: Acclaimed filmmaker Cheryl Dunye takes centre stage in this ode to love, community and the past.

movies.title: Vampyr
movies.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer’s 1932 film is a founding and defining works of psychological horror cinema.

movies.title: Days of Heaven
movies.description: Richard Gere plays a Chicagoan trying to make a new life in the country and finding that love gets in the way.

movies.title: West Indies: The Fugitive Slaves of Liberty
A City of Sadness
movies.description: Hou Hsiao-Hsien breached political taboos in his Golden Lion-winning tale of a Taiwanese family in the mid-1940s.

movies.title: All about My Mother
movies.description: Pedro Almodóvar's dazzling study of grief, motherhood and female solidarity.

movies.title: Amarcord
movies.description: Federico Fellini returned for inspiration to his own childhood in 1930s Rimini for this colourful comedy-drama about life in a small seaside town under Fascist rule.

movies.title: Ikiru
movies.description: This study of a terminally ill civil servant seeking meaning in his life is one of Japanese director Akira Kurosawa’s finest achievements.

movies.title: Los olvidados
movies.description: Luis Buñuel’s searingly powerful account of the brutalised lives of delinquent Mexico City street kids fuses stark realism with surrealist flourishes.

movies.title: Once upon a Time in America
Orlando
movies.country: United Kingdom, Russian Federation, Italy, France, Netherlands
movies.description: Tilda Swinton stars in Sally Potter's dazzling interpretation of Virginia Woolf's novel.

movies.title: The Gospel According to St. Matthew
movies.description: Pier Paolo Pasolini’s third feature abandons the profane in favour of the sacred in a documentary-like retelling of the story of Christ.

movies.title: Vivre sa vie
movies.description: Jean-Luc Godard’s fourth feature – his third with wife and muse Anna Karina – charts in 12 tableaux a would-be actress’s descent into prostitution.

movies.title: Black Narcissus
movies.description: Tensions grow when a group of nuns open a convent in the Himalayas in Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger’s remarkable melodrama.

movies.title: Charulata
movies.description: Satyajit Ray’s sublime portrait of a bored housewife living in 19th-century Bengal.

movies.title: Heat
movies.description: Michael Mann’s virtuoso cat-and-mouse thriller starring Al Pacino and Robert De Niro.

movies.title: L'Argent
movies.description: Robert Bresson’s last film turns a Tolstoy novella about a forged banknote into a formidably focused meditation on the supposed root of all evil.

movies.title: Last Year at Marienbad
movies.description: In Alain Resnais’ infamous art-house teaser, from a screenplay by Alain Robbe-Grillet, a male guest at a chateau claims he met a woman there the year before.

movies.title: Letter from an Unknown Woman
movies.description: Max Ophuls brought his trademark flowing camera style and a taste of the old Vienna to Hollywood for this tragic story of unrequited love.

movies.title: Memories of Underdevelopment
movies.description: A complex character study of alienation amid tumultuous social change, from one of Cuba’s greatest filmmakers.

movies.title: Red Desert
movies.description: Michelangelo Antonioni's mid-career masterpiece stars Monica Vitti as an emotionally anguished young woman embarking on a tentative affair with a businessman (Richard Harris).

movies.title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
The Magnificent Ambersons
movies.description: Among the most famous of broken films, Orson Welles’ masterful follow-up to Citizen Kane was taken out of his control and re-edited by the studio.

movies.title: Un chien andalou
movies.description: A scabrous study of desire, the subconscious and anti-clericalism – Luis Buñuel and Salvador Dalí’s provocative first film is a classic of Surrealist cinema.

movies.title: Under the Skin
movies.description: An alien Scarlett Johansson prowls the streets of Glasgow in Jonathan Glazer’s astonishing, mind-bending mixture of existential science fiction and inner-city realism.

movies.title: An Autumn Afternoon
movies.description: Yasujirō Ozu’s final film colourfully and emotionally revisits the themes of Late Spring.

movies.title: Greed
movies.description: Silent cinema’s most famous ‘lost’ film, Erich von Stroheim’s monumental study of three ordinary lives destroyed by avarice was ruinously edited down by the studio.

movies.title: Les Demoiselles de Rochefort
movies.description: Jacques Demy’s follow-up to Les Parapluies de Cherbourg is a joyous, large-scale tribute to the Hollywood musical.

movies.title: Magnolia
movies.description: Paul Thomas Anderson's sprawling, intense and multi-layered study of a collection of characters going through varying levels of crisis.

movies.title: Paris, Texas
movies.country: Federal Republic of Germany, France, United Kingdom
movies.description: Harry Dean Stanton's finest role came as the near-mute Travis, on a journey across America to reunite his family, in Wim Wenders’ tale of loss and redemption.

movies.title: Pyaasa
movies.description: Guru Dutt’s classic, set in post-independence Kolkata (then Calcutta), tells of a young poet’s ambition.

movies.title: Ran
movies.description: Made late in his career, the last of Akira Kurosawa’s great historical epics transposes the story of Shakespeare’s King Lear to feudal Japan.

movies.title: The Birds
movies.description: Birds inexplicably turn against man and begin attacking the small community of Bodega Bay, in Alfred Hitchcock’s suspense classic.

movies.title: The River
movies.description: Jean Renoir's intoxicating first colour feature is a lyrical adaptation of Rumer Godden's coming-of-age tale of an adolescent girl living with her English family on the banks of West Bengal.

movies.title: Wings of Desire
movies.description: In director Wim Wenders’ most metaphysical work, a guardian angel desires nothing more than to be human.

movies.title: Double Indemnity
movies.description: An insurance salesman (Fred MacMurray) is seduced into murder and fraud in Billy Wilder’s classic dark thriller, adapted from the novel by James M. Cain.

movies.title: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
movies.description: Peter Sellers plays three separate roles in Stanley Kubrick’s mordant Cold War comedy in which insanity and political manoeuvrings lead to nuclear meltdown.

movies.title: I Know Where I’m Going!
movies.description: Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger’s heady romantic masterpiece.

movies.title: L' eclisse
movies.description: Michelangelo Antonioni’s film charts the hot and cold relationship of a young couple in bustling Rome.

movies.title: Nosferatu
movies.description: Cinema’s original vampire movie, this copyright-infringing adaptation of Bram Stoker’s Dracula is one of the great classics of German expressionist cinema.
